briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 11, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Record Heatwaves and Droughts: A Global Emergency
sections.content: Last month, ocean temperatures reached an all-time high, while Western Europe experienced its worst heatwave [1, 37]. In the United States, July was the hottest month on record [235], and an Amber Heat-Health Alert was issued for most of England [232, 236]. Domestically, severe heatwaves reaching 40 degrees Celsius have led to delivery riders collapsing from heat exhaustion [201], and the total electricity demand due to heatwaves has hit an all-time high, increasing pressure for electricity bill hikes [25]. Human casualties and economic losses are significant [15, 46]. Furthermore, extreme weather events are occurring simultaneously worldwide, with Typhoon 'Dolphin' striking Shanghai, China, and heavy rainfall forecast for Beijing [202] [41, 210, 219]. Concurrently, 17 cities and counties in the Gyeongnam region have entered a severe drought phase [203], and Parmigiano cheese production in Italy is under threat [208, 230], demonstrating the widespread impacts of climate change.

sections.title: 🇰🇷🌱 Domestic Policies for Climate Change Adaptation and the Spread of Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, the establishment of institutional foundations for climate change adaptation is active. The 'Climate Crisis Adaptation Bill' has passed the bill review subcommittee of the National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate, promoting strengthened support for climate-vulnerable groups and regions, and the activation of 'climate insurance' [21, 100, 122]. Local governments and the education sector are also continuing various efforts to achieve carbon neutrality. The Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education has declared a major educational transformation to realize carbon neutrality in schools and is collaborating with civil society [53, 56, 59, 60, 61, 70, 73, 74, 75, 76, 83, 84, 85, 92, 94, 99, 105, 106, 107, 108, 109, 114, 116, 118, 124]. Various local governments, including Gwacheon City, Gimcheon City, and Wanju County, are promoting carbon neutrality in daily life through resident action groups, campaigns, and education [49, 50, 51, 52, 54, 55, 62, 64, 66, 68, 69, 71, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 86, 87, 90, 91, 95, 97, 98, 101, 103, 110, 115, 117, 119, 121, 123]. Furthermore, region-specific climate change responses are actively underway, such as attempts to restore seaweed beds in Jeju through experimental transplantation of *Sargassum horneri* [7, 9, 14, 18], and operating cooling patrol vehicles to locate elderly individuals working alone in the heatwave using drones [205].

sections.title: 🌱🇰🇷 Regulatory Improvements and Investment Reinforcement for Expanding Renewable Energy Supply
sections.content: To expand the supply of renewable energy, the government has introduced a national cap on separation distance regulations, which were previously applied differently by region to prevent disorderly development [125, 131, 132, 133, 137, 139, 141, 143, 144, 145, 147, 150, 151, 154, 158, 159, 163, 168, 171, 174, 180, 184, 185, 187, 188, 191, 192, 194, 196]. Consequently, the separation distance for solar power facilities is limited to a maximum of 200m from residential areas, and for wind power facilities to a maximum of 1500m, which is expected to ease the acquisition of development sites [145, 159, 163, 171]. There has also been a change where the term 'new and renewable energy' has disappeared from use after 22 years, with renewable energy and hydrogen now treated as independent policy subjects [126, 134]. Naju City demonstrated its leading role by achieving an 'A grade' in the top 10% nationwide for its new and renewable energy integrated support project [128, 135, 136, 138, 140, 142, 148, 149, 155, 156, 162, 167, 173, 175, 181, 183, 186]. Meanwhile, Chungnam Development Corporation and KEPCO KDN plan to return up to 50% of the power generation profits to local communities by promoting solar power generation projects utilizing idle public land [157, 172, 189, 193, 195, 198]. However, the Honam region is experiencing a surge in renewable energy output curtailment, bringing grid issues to the forefront as a government challenge [204], highlighting the urgent need for a stable power supply network.

sections.title: 🌍📰 Widespread Economic and Social Impacts of Climate Change and International Challenges
sections.content: Climate change is also leading to financial losses. Hanwha Life projects losses due to climate change to reach 2.2 trillion won by 2050 and is preparing phased asset management [6]. The increase in medical expenses and surge in insurance claims due to heatwaves illustrate a facet of the 'trillion-dollar bill' that climate change will bring [15, 46]. Internationally, warnings have emerged that the advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology could increase fossil fuel productivity, leading to higher carbon emissions [22]. China, despite its carbon neutrality declaration, is increasing its reliance on coal [48, 89, 111], suggesting difficulties for international carbon reduction efforts. Furthermore, the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) plans to discontinue support for its Arctic climate change report [209], and the Iran war has exposed failures in U.S. energy policy, raising the need for renewable energy cooperation with China [164]. These developments underscore how climate change is exacerbating complex security crises and the necessity for international cooperation [212, 226]. In this context, the opinion has also been raised that the productive financial transformation of private finance is essential to achieve 2050 carbon neutrality [113].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing for August 11, 2026. We look forward to seeing you at the next briefing.
